parsed.why: National passport, entry-screening, and custody exposures remain serious. State courts have repeatedly blocked enacted facility and document restrictions, offering a meaningful local mitigation, though other hostile measures and limited visitor-specific protection remain.

The national framework already creates substantial exposure; this state adds an operative birth-sex facility rule across public buildings, private bounty suits, and invalidation of state IDs. These direct, recurring exposures outweigh its nondiscrimination protections.

The national framework remains restrictive, but this state has broad operating nondiscrimination and hate-crime protections, shield measures, and no documented local facility ban or trans-specific targeting. These protections materially improve on the national baseline.

National document and facility exposures still apply. State protections against discrimination and hate crimes are enacted, with no documented local visitor-facing restrictions; the advisory sports resolution and unrepealed, unenforced sodomy statute are secondary concerns.

The state’s protective laws and shield measures improve on the national baseline, but do not displace national passport, entry, and facility rules. A documented birth-sex prison placement is concerning, though it is a dated custody incident, not routine visitor exposure.
